name: system-tracker
description: See how your Node.js app is used: page views, API calls, live connections and more, counted by the second up to the year, with a built-in dashboard and no tracking code in your routes.
author: codezeros

scripts.build: rm -rf dist && tsc && node scripts/copy-assets.js dist && node scripts/obfuscate-dist.js
scripts.prepublishOnly: npm run release:check && npm run release:bump && npm run build && npm run prepublish-release
scripts.postpublish: npm run postpublish-release && npm run public-postpublish-release
scripts.release:check: test "$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" = main || { echo "Release from the main branch"; exit 1; }; npm whoami >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Log in to npm (npm login) first"; exit 1; }; ! npm view "$npm_package_name" name >/dev/null 2>&1 || npm owner ls "$npm_package_name" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^$(npm whoami 2>/dev/null) " || { echo "Log in to npm (npm login) as an owner of $npm_package_name first"; exit 1; }
